description: Somos estudiantes de Tecnologías de la Información de la Universidad Técnica de Machala (Ecuador), apasionados por la programación y la ciencia de datos. Trabajamos en "The Earth Information Jukebox": un globo terráqueo 3D interactivo que convierte datos reales de la NASA sobre el cambio climático en sonido y visuales en tiempo real, para hacer la ciencia de la Tierra accesible y multisensorial.
summary: Earth Jukebox transforms NASA Earth Information Center visualizations into an interactive musical experience. The project pairs NASA’s global sea surface current and temperature visualization with real-time sonification: as a playhead scans the map from west to east, ocean colors are interpreted as estimated temperature and mapped to musical pitch, while areas without mapped ocean information remain silent. Users can explore different dates and hear how the resulting soundscape changes with Earth’s ocean conditions. The project also includes a climate-record mode using NASA GISTEMP data for global and Ecuador-focused exploration. Earth Jukebox aims to make Earth science more accessible and engaging by adding an auditory dimension to scientific visualization.
details:
Earth Jukebox is an interactive web application designed for NASA’s Earth Information Jukebox challenge. It combines NASA Earth Information Center visualizations with real-time sonification so users can experience scientific information through both sight and sound.

The main experience uses NASA’s Global Sea Surface Currents and Temperature visualization (SVS 3912), produced from ECCO2 model output. We selected 48 frames spanning March 25, 2007 to March 3, 2008. Each frame is displayed as a global ocean map. During playback, a playhead scans the visualization from west to east. Ocean color is interpreted as an estimated sea surface temperature and mapped to musical pitch using a pentatonic scale. Areas without sufficient mapped ocean information remain silent. The result is a different soundscape for different dates.

The application also includes a Climate Record mode using NASA GISTEMP data, with global and Ecuador-focused views, allowing users to explore long-term temperature anomalies.

The application was built with React, Vite, JavaScript, globe.gl, and Tone.js. It runs in the browser and does not require a backend or external API during the experience.

The core creative concept was defined by the team: translating the visual scan of NASA ocean data into sound. Super Intelligence tools were used to accelerate implementation, debugging, testing, and documentation, while the team defined the creative mapping and final experience.

The project is intended to make Earth science more accessible, memorable, and multisensory by giving users a way to listen to changes in scientific visualizations rather than only viewing them.
